A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EXPRESS-Bench, Fine-EQA and the EAC metric. All 18 pages of each version, including the supplementary sections, equations, figures and tables, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original EXPRESS-Bench experiments, component ablations, human comparisons, and exploration and answer-faithfulness analyses in the main text and supplement.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds external-benchmark evaluations, VLM ablations and ambiguity measurements. Its original results are distinguishable from the explicitly borrowed OpenEQA baseline scores.

M1.justification: Fine-EQA's semantic maps, frontier/goal exploration switching, stopping procedure and answer generation remain unchanged in Sections 4 and 7. Naming the Prismatic checkpoint clarifies implementation; the alternative answering VLMs are ablation configurations rather than a revised proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: v1's evaluations use EXPRESS-Bench. v3 Section 5.3 adds OpenEQA's active A-EQA subset and HM-EQA, extending evaluation beyond the proposed benchmark and adding multiple-choice question answering alongside open-ended answering.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds GPT-4o-mini-captioned Socratic variants of DeepSeek-V3, GPT-4 and LLaMA-3-8b while retaining their LLaVA-captioned counterparts. New comparisons also introduce quoted OpenEQA/GPT-4V results and an evaluated Explore-EQA comparator, substantially expanding the comparison methods.

E3.justification: The added evaluations introduce OpenEQA's C' and E' scoring protocol, documented in Supplement Section 8.2.1, and HM-EQA accuracy and navigation-path-length metrics. Table 3 compares Fine-EQA on the full question set with borrowed GPT-4V results on 184 questions. VLM substitution adds configuration controls; the existing EXPRESS-Bench protocol is retained.

E4.justification: v3 extends the analyses to dependence on the answering VLM, replacing GPT-4o-mini with Janus-Pro-7B and Qwen-Vl-Plus in Table 6. It also adds a cross-dataset question-ambiguity analysis in Section 5.3. Existing exploration-module ablations, category analyses and trajectory/confidence case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Unlike v1, v3 displays uncertainty values: Table 3 reproduces 41.8 ± 3.2 and 7.5 ± 0.6 for the borrowed OpenEQA/GPT-4V baseline. This is a limited addition to reporting, with no newly reported seeds, repeated-run counts or uncertainty estimates for Fine-EQA's own results.

E6.justification: Existing EXPRESS-Bench values remain unchanged, including Fine-EQA's C=40.55 and Epath=16.22. v3 adds caption-baseline, external-benchmark and VLM-ablation results. Table 4 reports Fine-EQA accuracy/path length of 56.0%/54.267 m versus Explore-EQA's 50.4%/93.687 m. New ambiguity rates are 35.6%, 62.3% and 9.7% for HM-EQA, OpenEQA and EXPRESS-Bench. The OpenEQA comparison uses unequal question sets.

T1.justification: The proposed method equations, EAC definitions and existing supplementary metrics are unchanged. The added C' and E' equations document the adopted OpenEQA scoring convention; they do not introduce new theoretical reasoning, assumptions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same principal claims: EXPRESS-Bench with 777 trajectories and 2,044 question-trajectory pairs, hybrid Fine-EQA exploration, and EAC assessment. The additional experiments support these retained contributions without redefining them.

C2.justification: v3 attributes OpenEQA's exploration inefficiency to frontier-only navigation and delayed termination. It also interprets the VLM ablation as a tradeoff between answer correctness and exploration efficiency. These are new mechanism interpretations; the existing human-performance gap and weakness on existence questions remain.

D1.justification: v3 identifies the previously generic Prismatic VLM as Prism-DINOSigLIP 7B. Section 3.2 also clarifies that manual question refinement includes object locations, attributes and relationships. These are additional disclosures, without evidence that the original dataset or implementation was changed; existing prompts, exploration limits and repository access information are retained.

R1.justification: The bibliography and Related Work section remain unchanged. New Section 5.3 sharpens positioning against already-cited OpenEQA and Explore-EQA, including a specific criticism of OpenEQA's exploration and stopping behavior. This is a limited extension of the relationship to existing research.

P1.justification: v3 inserts an external-dataset experiments subsection, expands the ablation discussion, and makes localized edits to filtering and baseline descriptions. Subsequent experiment subsections are renumbered, and some supplementary paragraphs move. The overall structure and most existing prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains three rows, and new Tables 3, 4 and 6 display external-benchmark and VLM-ablation results. Original Tables 3 and 4 become Tables 5 and 7 and move within the experiments section. Figure 8's caption expands; existing figure content and the overall layout style are retained.

improvement.justification: External-benchmark evaluations, stronger captioning baselines and VLM substitutions broaden the empirical support and probe dependence on GPT-4o-mini. The gain is limited by the unequal OpenEQA evaluation sets, unspecified ambiguity-measurement procedure and absence of uncertainty estimates for the authors' results. These additions provide a useful but bounded improvement while preserving the original method and findings.
